analysis.title: Global Asset Allocation: Underweight US Equities (November 2026)
key_insights: TS Lombard cuts global equities to underweight, takes alternatives to neutral and rebuilds cash. The 12m portfolio beta falls to 0.92 from 1.07. The stated drivers are a more hawkish Fed, sticky US services inflation, a fiscal drag next year and a peak in hyperscaler capex growth rates.

US equities go to underweight (-0.5pp vs benchmark) after a 350bp cut. The house view is that the Fed will hike more than the market expects, with a quarterly hike path and a 5% terminal rate. Falling energy prices only temper this at the margin.

US earnings growth may be peaking. Slower capex growth, resistance to data-centre construction, fiscal drag, stronger wage growth and higher rates are the cited headwinds. Hyperscaler gains on stakes in AI companies could also reverse and stop flattering earnings growth.

The US equity cut is recycled into the euro area. Germany (+250bp), France (+150bp), Italy (+50bp) and Spain (+150bp) are added, and Spain is the largest European overweight at +1.5pp. The reasons given are lower energy prices, a recovery in European bank stocks and less US political and trade uncertainty. The UK goes back to neutral.

India is rebuilt (+300bp in the portfolio) on lower oil prices, an accelerating credit impulse, bottoming PMIs and a market still down year to date. China is cut further and becomes the largest equity underweight because of weak domestic macro, rich earnings expectations and breadth that is not yet weak enough to signal a buy.

Taiwan is trimmed (-200bp) but stays overweight. Higher rates and doubts over AI economics weigh on capex expectations. TSMC's order book is strong and GPU rental rates suggest AI demand remains firm, so the house keeps a toe in the AI trade after the Tech sell-off.

Health Care is upgraded to strong overweight. The indicator is now led by pharma output, with sustained M&A and Eli Lilly's first approved weight-loss pill as support. Energy equities are cut from overweight to neutral in the body text, though a summary bullet says underweight. Crude flows from the Persian Gulf have normalised and crack spreads are falling.

Duration stays at maximum underweight. UST 10y yields fell to 4.84% on midterm day during an AI scare, then rose back above 5% after October payrolls and a hot CPI report. The market now prices roughly three more hikes by end-2027, which TS Lombard says is still below its own hike path.

Government bonds: UST and JGB views move from 0 to -1. The 10y JGB is expected to head back above 3% unless AI panic returns, because wage growth, output price surveys and the Tankan support a BoJ terminal rate of at least 2%. The portfolio adds BTPs (+150bp) and BONOs (+100bp) and cuts USTs (-100bp).

Brazil local debt is cut sharply (-600bp) after heavy losses, which were the main driver of the model portfolio's -4.95% month. Brazil government bonds move to +1 from +2 and BRL to -1 from +1. The carry and capital gain case still holds on fiscal consolidation and weak growth, but FX is the main risk.

The dollar view is bullish. The in-house dollar bull/bear indicator is at its strongest since 2023 and still rising. Lower energy prices are not seen as dollar bearish because softer BoE and ECB rhetoric could widen rate differentials. A Brent move closer to $70 would be needed to restore a global reacceleration regime in FX.

FX changes: CHF to -2 from -1 (widening rate differentials), INR to +1 from -1 (lower fuel prices), BRL to -1 from +1. EUR stays at -1 and AUD stays at -1. KRW and CNY are the best placed EM currencies against further dollar gains, and MXN is more resilient than other LatAm currencies after a positioning shakeout. The text is inconsistent on INR, saying 0 in one place.

Credit tilts to high yield for shorter duration. Global HY is raised +250bp and the credit underweight narrows by 200bp. EM sovereign credit is cut -50bp and EM local debt is cut -6.0pp because of dollar risk.

Alternatives are cut by 6.0pp to benchmark. Industrial metals go to -1 on Fed tightening, weak Chinese fixed-asset investment and roadblocks to US data-centre buildout after Democratic gubernatorial wins. Precious metals go to -1 on rising real yields and negative ETF and PBoC buying momentum. Managed futures are trimmed as Iran escalation risk fades. Cash rises 10.3pp to 14.0%.

Style tilts are unchanged. Cyclicals vs Defensives stays neutral because the risk allocation index does not yet support a full rotation, and Defensives have rallied hard, including Staples without earnings support. The house keeps a weak preference for Tech over Traditional Cyclicals, expressed only through Taiwan.

sector_views.rationale: Upgraded to strong overweight. The indicator is led by pharma output and points to outperformance into early 2027, with sustained M&A and Eli Lilly's first approved weight-loss pill as support. EPS trends remain strong.

Cut from overweight. Persian Gulf crude flows have normalised, crack spreads are declining and the Iran conflict is seen as less likely to escalate for long, so the bull market for energy stocks could be over. A summary bullet says underweight.

Weak preference for Tech over Traditional Cyclicals, expressed only via Taiwan. Tech has sold off sharply and the Tech risk appetite indicator is the weakest since 2022, while GPU rental rates point to strong AI demand.
The risk allocation index does not support a full rotation into Defensives. Defensives have rallied strongly in recent weeks and the Staples rally is not backed by earnings trends.

earnings_insights: US EPS growth is forecast to slow next year (TS Lombard view, not a printed figure). Cited reasons are slower capex growth, fiscal drag, stronger wages and higher rates.
TSMC revenue reported up 43% y/y over the first ten months of the year. The order book is described as strong and revenue growth is still accelerating.
Neocloud earnings were described as stronger than expected, which helped revive AI sentiment. No figures are given.
Hyperscaler capex growth rates are seen as peaking (house view). Capex growth estimates are no longer rising.
Healthcare EPS trends are described as strong. Chinese earnings growth expectations are described as already rich.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Payrolls accelerated, which the report reads as the US labour market reaccelerating and supporting more Fed tightening.

macro_indicators.reading: 0.3% MoM, third month in a row
macro_indicators.interpretation: An all-round hot CPI report pushed 10y UST yields back above 5% and reinforced the sticky services inflation view.
Yields round-tripped from the AI-scare low back to pre-scare Fed pricing.

macro_indicators.reading: About three more hikes priced by end-2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: TS Lombard says this is still below its own quarterly hike trajectory, so tightening risk is underpriced.
The house view is a more aggressive tightening campaign than the market expects, which is negative for US equities and EM assets.
A crude bear market after the midterms and a diplomatic turn on Iran. It supports euro area and India equities and EA periphery bonds.

macro_indicators.indicator: Brent crude threshold for FX regime change
macro_indicators.interpretation: FX markets would need a sharp drop toward this level to switch back into a global macro reacceleration mode.
Supports a view that the 10y JGB yield heads back above 3% unless AI panic returns.
Monetary policy outlook column in the allocation table. ECB rhetoric may soften with energy prices.
The Indian rate hike cycle has begun and further tightening is expected.

trade_ideas.description: Underweight US equities (-0.5pp vs benchmark after a 3.5pp cut), rotate into euro area equities led by Spain, France, Italy and Germany
trade_ideas.rationale: A more hawkish Fed, slowing US EPS growth and softer fuel prices that favour euro area equities.
trade_ideas.risk: A durable return of Iran escalation or a sharp rebound in energy prices.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Global High Yield credit (+250bp in the model portfolio) funded from other credit and EM sovereign credit
trade_ideas.rationale: Low duration of the HY index suits upside risks to US rates and US credit fundamentals remain benign.

trade_ideas.description: Keep duration at maximum underweight and prefer cash in US, Japan and euro area rates, while overweighting EA periphery govvies (BTPs, BONOs)
trade_ideas.rationale: Fed tightening risk is underpriced and a hawkish BoJ points to higher JGB yields, while dovish energy signals help periphery bonds.
trade_ideas.risk: A renewed AI panic would bring a bid for USTs and JGBs.

trade_ideas.description: Long USD vs CHF (-2), EUR (-1), AUD (-1) and BRL (-1), with KRW and CNY (+1) best placed against dollar strength
trade_ideas.rationale: Widening policy divergence with a more aggressive Fed and a strengthening dollar bull/bear indicator.
trade_ideas.risk: A sharp fall in Brent toward $70 could bring a global macro reacceleration regime that favours high beta FX.

trade_ideas.description: Strong overweight Health Care, with India rebuilt to benchmark and a modest Taiwan overweight kept as a toe in the AI trade
trade_ideas.rationale: Healthcare indicator and EPS trends are strong, India benefits from lower oil and a credit impulse, and Taiwan is supported by TSMC orders and GPU rental rates.
trade_ideas.risk: Continued AI capex cuts would hit Taiwan's hardware supply chain.

risk_factors: A more aggressive Fed tightening campaign than the market prices.
Slowing US EPS growth, a fiscal drag and a reversal of hyperscaler investment gains.
Renewed escalation in Iran, although the report sees it as less likely to last.
A return of AI panic, which would push USTs and JGBs higher in price and lower yields.
Further dollar strength, which pressures EM assets and EM local debt.
BRL depreciation despite carry and capital gains on Brazilian local bonds.
Chinese domestic macro deterioration and weak fixed-asset investment.
French fiscal weakness and euro area growth deceleration.
vol_and_positioning: The Tech risk appetite indicator is the weakest since 2022 after a sharp Tech sell-off.
The Risk Allocation Index has rolled over as earnings trends weaken.
The USD bull/bear indicator is at its strongest since 2023 and rising, and the dollar is described as breaking out.
EUR positioning is bearish but TS Lombard stays at -1 vs the dollar.
MXN has seen a positioning shakeout, in contrast with BRL, which supports relative MXN resilience.
ETF and PBoC gold purchase trackers show negative momentum.
China market breadth has weakened sharply but is not yet at a level that signals a clear buy.
Semiconductors are now a very large share of the US IT index.
geopolitical: Iran conflict is described as stuck in a pattern of mutual siege with periodic flare-ups. Munitions shortages and casualty intolerance should push Trump toward negotiation.
US midterm results (a GOP defeat) reduce the chance of renewed escalation lasting long. JD Vance's post-vote tweet put the Iran war at the top of the list of reasons for the loss.
Trump has signalled willingness to work with the Democrats, which the report expects to lower geopolitical and trade uncertainty.
Persian Gulf crude flows across Hormuz are back at pre-war levels per Kpler data, and LNG flows are near 50% of pre-war levels. Refined product supply remains tight.
Democratic gubernatorial victories in states with a large share of planned US data-centre capacity create new roadblocks to AI infrastructure buildout.
Beijing's effort to support the stock market through company share buybacks has so far failed to revive sentiment.

tension_points.bull_case: GPU rental prices are rising across several generations, neocloud earnings beat expectations and TSMC revenue is up 43% y/y over ten months, so AI demand remains very strong.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscaler capex growth rates appear to have peaked, resistance to data-centre construction is growing and higher rates raise doubts over AI economics.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A switch back into AI panic mode, which would push JGB yields lower and cut the Taiwan overweight rationale.

tension_points.bull_case: Lower energy prices reduce the chance of prolonged escalation in Iran and should lift high beta FX and euro area assets.
tension_points.bear_case: Softer energy prices may lead the BoE and ECB to sound less hawkish, widening rate differentials against the US and supporting the dollar.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharp decline in Brent closer to the $70/bbl range would switch FX markets back into a global macro reacceleration mode.

tension_points.bull_case: Munitions shortages, casualty intolerance and midterm electoral pressure should push Trump toward negotiation, and Gulf crude flows are already at pre-war levels.
tension_points.bear_case: The conflict has had periodic flare-ups and refined product supply remains tight, so risk premia could return.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The durability of the improvement depends on the odds of a more durable US-Iran solution, and a renewed air-strike campaign would reverse it.

theme_stances.evidence: A more hawkish Fed is the biggest risk to equities.

theme_stances.key_argument: Slower capex growth, fiscal drag, stronger wages and higher rates mean US EPS growth could disappoint next year.
theme_stances.evidence: We could be looking at peak US earnings growth.

theme_stances.theme: rotation from US to euro area equities
theme_stances.key_argument: Softer fuel prices, a bank stock recovery and lower political uncertainty favour euro area equities over US equities.
Hawkish US data pose a risk of a more aggressive Fed tightening campaign and widen policy divergence.
